body.title: Make the activation tests run to completion
body.reproduction:
1. On main (a66eae5a), run the activation test file alone: `cd vscode-plugin && npx tsx --test src/__tests__/activation.test.ts` (Node 22, macOS).
2. Observed: 6 tests, 1 pass, 0 fail, 5 cancelled. 'runReachabilityProbe degrades a hung probe to errored within the bounded deadline' is cancelled with 'Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved', and the four tests after it are cancelled too ('never throws even if reachability() rejects', 'activateExtension returns synchronously ...', 'the extension package is scaffolded ...', 'only extension.ts imports vscode ...'). The same 5 are cancelled in the full plugin suite.

Expected: all six tests run and report pass or fail.
body.rootCause: runReachabilityProbe (vscode-plugin/src/activation.ts:34-58) races the daemon probe against a deadline promise. The deadline's setTimeout is deliberately unref()'d, with the comment 'Do not keep the process alive for the probe (Node hosts / tests)'. The hung-probe test passes a probe that never settles and a 20 ms deadline. While it awaits, the only pending work is that unref'd timer, which does not keep the event loop alive. The loop drains before the timer fires, and node:test reports the test as still pending and cancels it together with the tests that have not run yet. (This is diagnosed from the code and the error message; it has not yet been confirmed by a change.) In the VS Code extension host the event loop is kept alive by the host, so the product behaviour is not affected. Neither the test file nor activation.ts has changed since 2026-09-24 (9bb8c6f3); when the file started failing is not determined.
body.fixIntent: The hung-probe test must keep the process alive long enough for the probe's deadline to fire, or otherwise stop depending on the unref'd timer, without changing the product's choice not to keep a host alive. All six tests in the file then run and report, so the five activation-shell checks they cover (deadline, never-throws, synchronous activation, package scaffold, the vscode-import boundary) are actually exercised again.

citations.quotedText: timer = setTimeout(() => resolve('errored'), timeoutMs); // Do not keep the process alive for the probe (Node hosts / tests). ... (timer as { unref(): unknown }).unref(); ... reachability = await Promise.race([deps.client.reachability(), deadline]);

test('runReachabilityProbe degrades a hung probe to errored within the bounded deadline', ...) ... await runReachabilityProbe({ client: hung, status, probeTimeoutMs: 20 }); assert.equal(status.current().state, 'errored');
